newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude edges up with WTI, ANS idles.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude edges up with WTI, ANS idles.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes pared early losses Monday afternoon, edging up with West Texas Intermediate cash (WTI) barrels while Alaska spot activity remained sluggish in typical early week doldrums.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude rose from the morning in line with a five-cent gain in WTI to hit $25.30/25.50.
But WTI, the basis for ANS, remained weaker than Friday levels, as the U.N. cleared an agreement for Iraq to export oil for food and weather turned milder in the U.S. Northeast.
ANS differentials added nothing to prices, as they remained flat at $1.75 under WTI.
Offers for Alaskan crude stayed $1.65 under WTI while buyers kept bids at $2.00 under.
Dealers said 12,000 bpd term deal of Argentine Rincon crude was sold to Unocal last week. The deal is set at 90 cents off February WTI and will last four months.
Tosco reportedly lost the bidding war for the Rincon, and 12,000 bpd of Rincon remains available in the spot market, traders said.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
Outright prices increased 30 cents to $18.00/18.10 a barrel after more oil companies reported posted price increases Monday.
Wilmington premiums stagnated at 55 to 65 cents over postings, but outright prices rose 20 cents on the increased postings.
